response.title: Is a robot mower without a wire realistic for a one-acre yard, or will it run out of battery before it finishes?
response.answer:
Yes, a wire-free robotic mower is absolutely realistic for a one-acre yard. Battery life usually isn't the problem. The more important question is whether the mower can cover the entire acre within a reasonable amount of time.

Modern robotic mowers are designed to automatically return to their charging station, recharge, and resume mowing. They don't need to finish your entire lawn on a single battery charge.

How a robot mower handles one acre
1–3 hrs

Typical mowing time per charge

Automatic

Recharging and resuming

Several days

Possible full coverage cycle

Illustrative ranges, not specifications for a particular model. Actual performance varies significantly.

Unlike a riding mower, which cuts your entire lawn once a week, a robotic mower generally maintains the grass by cutting a little at a time, often daily.

For example, a mower might cut part of your acre today, recharge, and continue tomorrow. As long as it keeps up with grass growth, your lawn stays consistently short.

What matters more than battery capacity

Rated coverage: Look for a model rated for at least 1 acre, preferably 1.25–1.5 acres to provide some margin.

Navigation: RTK GPS, camera-based vision, and LiDAR systems can eliminate perimeter wires, but differ in reliability around trees, buildings, and narrow passages.

Mowing efficiency: Systematic, straight-line mowing is generally more efficient than random navigation.

Terrain: Steep slopes, rough ground, and obstacles can significantly reduce coverage.

Charging and scheduling: A mower that can resume precisely where it stopped is especially useful on large properties.

Wire-free models worth considering

These are examples of mowers rated for approximately one acre or more, rather than smaller models that might struggle to keep up.

Rated for 1.25 acres, with all-wheel drive and RTK plus vision navigation. Worth considering for uneven terrain.

Worx Landroid Vision Cloud 9 in. 4WD Robot Lawn Mower (1 1/2…

$3,343.18

Rated for 1.5 acres, with four-wheel drive and RTK plus vision navigation.

For perspective, Kress specifies an average 85-minute runtime and 72-minute charging time for its 1.25-acre KR174 model. That illustrates how multiple mowing and charging sessions are an intended part of operating a large-lawn robot. 
KR174

One important distinction: a one-acre property isn't necessarily one acre of grass. If your house, driveway, patio, and landscaping occupy 0.3 acre, you only need to mow 0.7 acre.

Two questions that would help me recommend the right mower
How much of your property is actually grass?
Almost the entire acre
About ½–¾ acre
Less than ½ acre
What does the terrain look like?
Mostly flat and open
Flat, but lots of trees or obstacles
Hilly or uneven
Find the right mower for my yard

These details matter much more than whether the battery can last long enough to finish everything in one trip.
